prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant reports neck pain consistent with whiplash and states they are not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the collision occurred as described, and the other driver's statement matches. Scene photos show damage mostly in line with the described impact speed.

Entry 3: Claimant is named on the policy and was confirmed by the police report as the driver in the vehicle at the time. No prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 4: Claimant gave the same account of the collision in each conversation so far. No prior injury to the neck or upper back is known from the records reviewed.

Entry 5: Reported whiplash symptoms are plausible for an impact of this type. Treatment followed a usual course, with visits tapering as the claimant reported steady improvement.

Entry 6: Claim reviewed against all available evidence. Injury and vehicle damage both fit the described collision, and the file is ready for settlement review.
